title: A Vow for the Garden
premise: Zephyrine Sterling, a lighthouse keeper's grandson who writes romance novels under a woman's name, has spent seven years hiding from the town that blames his family for a fatal storm-night ferry accident. When the local library's anonymous pen-pal program pairs him with Wren Calloway—the coast guard officer leading the inquiry that could condemn his grandfather's memory—he answers under his pen name, never expecting honesty to bloom between them. As letters deepen into love, Wren discovers the truth, forcing Zephyrine to choose between silence that keeps him safe and testimony that might save the lighthouse but expose everything. In the end, he testifies, loses the lighthouse to decommissioning, and gains Wren, who stays after the last train leaves because some vows are kept in person.
about_author: Jude Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck records along the northern coast before turning to fiction. They write love stories for people who believe duty and desire can share a table, if neither insists on sitting at the head.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He tends the failing lighthouse, dodges the coast guard inquiry into the storm accident, and grudgingly joins the library's anonymous pen-pal program as research for his novel. His assigned correspondent turns out to be sharp-tongued, curious, and—unknown to her—his enemy. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace begins to crack.

chapters.title: Letters Written in Storm Light
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Through letters, Zephyrine (as 'Juniper') and Wren confess fears they'd tell no one face-to-face; meanwhile in person, their encounters bristle with professional hostility over the inquiry. The dramatic irony tightens as Wren quotes 'Juniper' back at Zephyrine without knowing it. Emotional beat: falling in love twice, in two directions, with one person.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cross-referencing handwriting on an old library card, Wren realizes Juniper is Zephyrine—and that his grandfather's logbook contains evidence contradicting the official storm report. Torn between duty and the man behind the letters, she confronts him at the lighthouse during a rising gale. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the harder question of what truth actually costs.

chapters.title: A Vow for the Garden
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At the inquiry's final hearing, he testifies using the recovered logbook, clearing his grandfather's name but ensuring the lighthouse's decommissioning anyway. He offers Wren an out; instead she boards down, plants a garden where the keeper's cottage stood, and stays past the last train. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into chosen love.
